newsitem.title: USA: Boeing/McDonnell trigger countdown on merger.
newsitem.headline: Boeing/McDonnell trigger countdown on merger.

text.p: Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp triggered a 20-day countdown to a government decision on their proposed $14 billion merger, a Boeing spokesman said Thursday.

The companies certified Wednesday that they have filed millions of pages of documents sought by the Federal Trade Commission to evaluate whether the merger meets requirements of the nation's antitrust laws.
The five-member FTC has until July 1 to make its decision. However, the countdown can be stopped at any time by mutual consent of the parties.
The clock would be reset if the FTC were to find the companies had failed to provide substantially all the documents it needs.
The merger would leave the combined company as one of only two manufacturers of large commercial aircfaft, competing with Airbus Industrie, the European consortium.
The timing is important because Boeing and McDonnell Douglas want the U.S. competition agency to rule before the European Union decides whether to approve the merger.
Boeing and others have operated on the assumption that the Americans are likely to be more favorable to the merger than the European Union.
The FTC is prohibited by law from commenting before it makes a decision. European competition officials have publicly raised doubts about the wisdom of the merger.
The European Union deadline for a ruling is at the end of July and cannot be extended.
